key_insight: A structured LLM workflow can automate the generation, validation, and tuning of multivariable process control designs directly from dynamic process models.
engineering_relevance: This could accelerate controller development for complex plants by producing executable decentralized control structures and tuning environments with less manual intervention.
method: Decompose control design into constrained code-generation steps: plant interface, normalization, MV-CV pairing, controller specification, simulation, scenario generation, and performance evaluation.
Validate each generated artifact before proceeding, and repair failures using feedback from the validation step.
Use Bayesian optimization to tune controller parameters against a closed-loop objective combining tracking and disturbance-rejection errors.
evidence_signal: On a nonlinear gas-preheater benchmark, Bayesian optimization reduced the closed-loop performance objective by about 26.5% versus the workflow’s initial controller, mainly by improving pressure-loop transients.
watch_item: The reported improvement is only for automated tuning on one benchmark, so broader validation on larger plantwide systems is still needed.
paper_title: An LLM-Driven Workflow for Automated Process Control Strategy Generation and Tuning from Dynamic Process Models
